lxc_fca23e7796a87679.text: Coffee beans begin inside a fruit.

lxc_16b76b16e3797982.text: You will follow coffee from a ripe cherry to a dry green bean.

lxc_d7d7e0d3798e318d.text: You will also compare Arabica and Robusta and learn three common processing methods.

lxc_872c43a148983755.text: Coffee grows on a plant as a small fruit called a coffee cherry.

lxc_43a92922ab4949cf.text: When many coffee cherries are ripe, they can be red or yellow, depending on the plant.

lxc_1f0dc54b6e1fa148.text: We call these seeds coffee beans because of their shape.

lxc_7b1f784ccd443966.text: After picking the cherries, producers remove some or all of the fruit and dry the seeds.

lxc_87e775db52d7130a.text: Before roasting, the dry seeds are called green coffee beans.

lxc_a8f0515ab8635ebe.text: They are usually pale green, not brown.

lxc_ce39ef491126b287.text: Roasting later changes their colour, smell, and flavour.

lxc_125518472e5ac81f.text: Arabica and Robusta are the two main commercial coffee species.

lxc_b88c21ee913f453e.text: Arabica is common in specialty cafés.

lxc_8e9cd9a1ad9dc9aa.text: It can have sweet, floral, fruity, or bright flavours.

lxc_3b3a8516d46039f0.text: The plants can be more difficult to grow and are often grown at higher places.

lxc_1381a3d6f3586e73.text: Their coffee often has more caffeine, stronger body, and more bitterness.

lxc_ecf2f1bee40e3fff.text: Some espresso blends use Robusta to add strength and body.

lxc_8b0f01e766f0f9e8.text: However, Robusta does not always mean bad coffee.

lxc_55c65460cd60c094.text: Careful farming, processing, and roasting can also produce high-quality Robusta.

lxc_b16d740e7d562c80.text: After picking, producers must separate and dry the coffee seeds.

lxc_0a41793c803036f0.text: In the washed process, machines remove the fruit before the seeds are fully dried.

lxc_c91148c03b739ce6.text: Water is often used during the process.

lxc_8e2f2663ad8ee4e8.text: Washed coffees are often known for clean flavours and clear differences between flavour notes.

lxc_d9c660fcfef96743.text: In the natural process, the whole coffee cherry dries around the seed.

lxc_87ab5083c85af385.text: Producers turn and watch the cherries carefully while they dry.

lxc_c3314485e7a0fc3d.text: Natural coffees can have stronger fruit, sweetness, or fermented flavours.

lxc_03db5eef22546451.text: If drying is not controlled well, the flavour can become unpleasant.

lxc_749e715c56c514f0.text: Honey processing is also called pulped-natural processing.

lxc_09c38e7e04b43af4.text: First, producers remove the outer skin and some fruit.

lxc_f66253cab650eac7.text: Some sticky fruit material stays on the seed while it dries.

lxc_f95554d423877693.text: This material can feel like honey, but producers do not add real honey to the coffee.

lxc_9eea18dbee12f7a0.text: The method sits between washed and natural processing.

lxc_52080b7e03b9c9fb.text: It can keep some clear flavours while adding sweetness or fruit character.

lxc_fbf9ebac3c961e3b.text: The exact result depends on the coffee, the amount of fruit left on the seed, the weather, and how carefully the producer controls drying.
